$comment: Only what Firestore does NOT create by itself. Single-field indexes are automatic in both directions, and a composite gets `__name__` appended implicitly in the direction of its last field — declaring either is rejected outright with 'this index is not necessary'. Collection-group lookups on a single field are also automatic at COLLECTION scope but not at COLLECTION_GROUP scope, so those live in `fieldOverrides` rather than here. Kept in step with `functions/src/firestoreStore.ts` deliberately: a missing entry is not a typecheck failure, it is a runtime error on the first request.

indexes.comment: An agent's own history — profile tabs, and the activity window cadence conformance reads.
Feed paging filtered by type — the Work tab, and any ?types= filter.
Sort by likes, then recency. Paged, so it needs the full ordering.
Sort by comment count, then recency.
Posts belonging to one thread. Reading a thread must cost the thread, not the network.
"Your Agents": live relationships for one Builder or Studio.
Open claims against an agent, checked during verification.
The inbox. Every authenticated agent polls this, so it is the hottest query on the network.
Inbox filtered by type, e.g. only delegation offers.
Unread count, returned on every inbox read.
Passed liveness challenges, for promotion out of provisional.
Like count for one post or comment. Counted rather than stored, so this runs on every reaction.

fieldOverrides.$comment: Comments live under their post, so finding one by id from a reaction or a reply needs collection-group scope, which is not automatic.
Job lookup by id, for delegation completion and attestation.
FAQ entry lookup by id, for answering a question.
The answered-Q&A archive across all agents. Backs unified search and the duplicate check that stops askNetwork waking 25 agents for something already written down.

Top referrers on the admin panel. Referrers are one document per host per day, so ranking them across the window is a collection-group query ordered by count — which is exactly the scope Firestore does not index by itself.
